columns.name: Andhra Pradesh & Bihar state each reported nearly 35 percent of total Rail-Road Accident in the country while Andhra Pradesh reported the highest incidence of these accidents during Ist four | number of Bihar reported the maximum 9 A.M. to 12’0 clock and 3.00 P.M. to respectively ‘Road Accidents’ were reported in the country while least number of these accidents (7.6%) were recorded during 000 to 0300 hours. The ‘Rail-Road Accidents’ were maximum during 0300 to 0600 hours (22.4%) followed by 0600 to 0900 hours (16.2%). The maximum number of ‘Railway Accidents’ were recorded during the pahars of 6 A.M. to 9 A.M. Amongst the 23 cities (with population of over 10 lakh), Bombay reported the maximum number of ‘Accidental Deaths’ (22.4%) followed by Delhi (17.3%). The rate of ‘Accidental Deaths’, however, was found to be highest at Indore (76.0%) followed by Nagpur (64.3%). The Bombay’s share of Accidental Deaths in all cities was in similar order as of Maharashtra in the country i.e. (22.8%). Expectantly the average rate of Accidental Deaths in cities (33.6) was higher than the All-India rate (23.6). Except 7 cities viz. Bhopal, Calcutta, Hyderabad, Kochi, Lucknow, Ludhiana and Madurai all other 16 cities also reported higher rate of ‘Accidental Deaths’ than the national average. It is also interesting to note that 12 out of 23 cities reported higher rate of ‘Accidental Deaths’ as compared to their parent Rate in Parent State
